guide.summary: Harvest time tracking, public app (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Greenhouse Harvest v3, partner OAuth (approval path unconfirmed); Greenhouse Harvest v3, customer-made credentials (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Easiest: Harvest time tracking, public app (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Greenhouse Harvest v3, customer-made credentials (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Composio lists Harvest as having managed OAuth. The dossier does not say whether the toolkit targets Harvest time tracking or Greenhouse Harvest; check the toolkit page.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio manages a Harvest OAuth app. For production you would want your own app so users see your brand and get dedicated quota. For Greenhouse Harvest that means a partnership.
reasons: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' on the managed app
Managed apps share rate-limit quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval
Default scopes may not cover everything you need

prerequisites.title: Confirm which Harvest you mean
prerequisites.detail: Harvest time tracking and Greenhouse's Harvest API are different products with different approval paths. The dossier covers both.

prerequisites.title: Harvest account with Developers access
prerequisites.detail: You create the OAuth2 app from the Developers section of Harvest ID.

prerequisites.title: Mutual customer and a website with privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Greenhouse requires at least one mutual customer, and an active website with a privacy policy. Without a Greenhouse customer there is no route into the partner program.

prerequisites.title: Business and legal inputs for the agreement
prerequisites.detail: The application needs a named mutual customer and may need revenue, security or compliance claims. These are decisions for you, not an agent.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI, register Harvest app
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. In Harvest ID Developers, create the OAuth2 app with name, redirect URL, Multi Account setting and products.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and secret

steps.title: Pick minimal products and scopes
steps.detail: Draft the minimal product scope (Harvest, Forecast or both) for the use case.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret, then test one user connection.
steps.done_when: A test account connects and a call succeeds

steps.title: Submit the integration request form
steps.detail: Submit Greenhouse's integration request form. Prepare a website with a privacy policy and name a mutual customer.

steps.title: Wait for monthly review and agreement
steps.detail: Greenhouse reviews on the first Monday of each month, then sends an API agreement. You may be refused.

steps.title: Draft credential request email
steps.detail: Draft the email with integration name, environment, exact scope strings, all final redirect URIs and a 128x128 logo.
steps.done_when: Email draft is ready to send

steps.title: Sign agreement and send request
steps.detail: Sign the agreement and send the request email to Partner Support.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config, confirm redirect
steps.detail: Create the auth config with the issued credentials. Tell Greenhouse the final working redirect URI once the callback is live.

steps.title: Write customer credential instructions
steps.detail: Draft steps for customers to create a Harvest v3 (OAuth) credential and share the ID and secret.

steps.title: Customer creates and hands over credential
steps.detail: Each customer's authorized user creates the credential and gives you the client ID and secret.

traps.title: Partner program needs a mutual customer
traps.detail: A pre-revenue product with no Greenhouse customer has no route into the partner program. Not every application is accepted.

traps.title: Redirect URIs and scopes are locked by email
traps.detail: You cannot edit redirect URIs yourself, and each change means another email and another wait. Partners cannot change their own scopes.

traps.title: Adding a scope forces re-authorization
traps.detail: Adding a scope requires every existing customer to re-authorize. Some scopes cannot be granted at all.

traps.title: Short token lifetimes
traps.detail: The authorization code lasts 1 minute and access tokens 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 14 days and rotate on each refresh, so an idle connection needs re-authorization.

traps.title: Customer permissions cap what you can do
traps.detail: Scopes are not sufficient on their own. List endpoints require a Site Admin authorizing user.

traps.title: Customer credentials have no refresh token
traps.detail: Request a new access token when the old one expires.

traps.title: Token lifetime differs between doc pages
traps.detail: The legacy V1 page says tokens expire in 18 hours; the V2 example shows 14 days. Use expires_in and refresh tokens, and do not hardcode a lifetime.

traps.title: Managed app limits
traps.detail: Composio's managed app shows Composio's name on the consent screen, shares quota and enforces 15-minute trigger polling. Fine for prototypes.

blockers.symptom: No self-serve client ID for Greenhouse Harvest v3
blockers.what_it_means: Partner OAuth credentials are issued only by Greenhouse after a signed agreement.
blockers.what_to_do: Apply through the integration request form, or use customer-created credentials (s3).
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the application and credential request email.

blockers.symptom: invalid_request: redirect_uri not configured for client_id
blockers.what_it_means: The redirect URI does not exactly match one registered with Greenhouse.
blockers.what_to_do: Email Partner Support to register the correct URI.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the URI against the registered list.

blockers.what_it_means: The customer user who authorized lacks the needed Greenhouse permissions.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer to re-authorize with a user (ideally a Site Admin) who has the permission.

open_questions: Which Harvest does the Composio 'harvest' toolkit target (getharvest.com or Greenhouse)? Check the toolkit page at docs.composio.dev/toolkits/harvest.
Does Harvest time tracking review or restrict apps before outside users connect? No review was found; check Harvest's developer docs or ask Harvest support.
Does Composio support Greenhouse customer-created client-credentials? Ask Composio support.
Do Harvest time tracking or Greenhouse have any app-specific user caps or hard rate limits? Greenhouse publishes none; ask Harvest and Partner Support.
Is a paid Greenhouse tier needed for sandbox testing? Sources conflict (Pro vs Expert); verify against the actual plan.
Not found: what each review or verification checks and what the developer must submit. Checked getharvest.com, github.com.

evidence.answer: For customer-created credentials, go to Configure > Dev Center > API Credential Management > Create new API credentials.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: When creating customer credentials, choose API type Harvest v3 (OAuth), then save and configure scopes.

evidence.answer: The OAuth authorize endpoint is GET https://auth.greenhouse.io/authorize with response_type, client_id, redirect_uri and scope parameters.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Create the credential from an ISU account, not a person's account.
evidence.answer: The credential should be created from an Integration Service User account, not a person's account, because a credential tied to an individual dies when that person is deactivated.

evidence.answer: Client secret rotation generates a new secret in the credential's client-secret tab, and the old one remains usable for a while.
